sentence: POST/PUT /api/journal with a body starting with or consisting of a NUL character returns 500 because the SQLite length CHECK fails with an unhandled IntegrityError.
evidence: Logged in via POST /api/auth/login as the demo user and sent the requests with curl. POST /api/journal {plant_id:1, entry_on:'2026-01-01'} with body '\u0000x', '\u0000' and '\u0000abc' each returned 'Internal Server Error' [500]. body 'x\u0000y' returned 201 (NUL in the middle is accepted). Then PUT /api/journal/4 with body '\u0000x' also returned 500. The test entry was deleted afterwards (204). Code: schemas.JournalEntryIn checks only min_length=1/max_length=500 in Pydantic, but db.py has CHECK (length(body) BETWEEN 1 AND 500). SQLite length() on TEXT counts characters only up to the first NUL, so a leading NUL makes the length 0 and the CHECK fails. routers/journal.py does not catch sqlite3.IntegrityError and there is no exception handler, so the server returns an unhandled 500 instead of a 4xx validation error.
